methodology.coldRunIsolation: Each run creates a fresh isolated CDP BrowserContext (Target.createBrowserContext), disables network cache (Network.setCacheDisabled), clears browser cache, and disposes the context after capture.
methodology.clsMeasurementWindow: Phase 1 (initial_load): navigation start through Page.loadEventFired, document.fonts.ready, initial-viewport images complete, plus post-load settle (2200ms on / to include offline catalog Suspense fallback resolution; 700ms on static routes). Phase 2 (scroll_pass): stepped scroll from y=0 to scrollHeight in 0.75*innerHeight increments (260ms dwell + finite animation completion wait) and return to y=0.
methodology.lcpMeasurementWindow: Captured via buffered PerformanceObserver('largest-contentful-paint') initialized via Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument and snapshotted immediately before the programmatic scroll pass so below-the-fold scroll images do not overwrite initial-load LCP.
methodology.interactionMeasurementProtocol: Trusted mouse events dispatched via CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent on fresh page loads per interaction, capturing both W3C PerformanceObserver('event', durationThreshold: 16) and PerformanceObserver('first-input') (which has no 16ms floor), alongside a double-rAF click-to-next-paint timing.

limitations: Synthetic headless-Chromium laboratory measurements on a single workstation are for controlled A/B comparison (Package A0 vs Package E) and are not equivalent to field CrUX telemetry or physical mobile hardware GPU profiling.

Chromium's W3C Event Timing 'event' observer enforces a minimum durationThreshold of 16ms; sub-16ms discrete interactions are captured via the W3C 'first-input' observer (8ms coarsened resolution) and a client double-rAF next-paint timer.
RequestAnimationFrame interval sampling in headless mode reflects software/headless compositor scheduling rather than physical mobile display refresh pacing.
FastAPI backend is intentionally offline per Frontend-First scope; '/' exercises the deterministic 1800ms catalog fallback path.
